info.description:
Scrobblr is a self-hosted music scrobbling service: it records what people
listen to and shows their listening, charts and what the community makes
of the catalog. This is its HTTP API: JSON over HTTPS, at the root of the
server's API address (written `https://scrobblr.example` below).

Besides this native API, the server speaks the protocols existing
scrobblers know: the Last.fm API, Audioscrobbler 1.2 and ListenBrainz
(the **Scrobbler protocols** section). An app that already scrobbles to
Last.fm or ListenBrainz usually needs only a different server URL.

## Getting started

Most reads are public: a profile, its charts, an artist's page, the
rankings.

```http
GET /v1/user/alice HTTP/1.1
Host: scrobblr.example
```

To act as a user, send a credential as a bearer token:

```http
GET /v1/user/me HTTP/1.1
Host: scrobblr.example
Authorization: Bearer 3d0b1f7c-1c2e-4f61-9a43-5d6e2b8f9a10
```

Times are RFC 3339 in UTC (`2026-10-13T10:41:07Z`), days are UTC dates
(`2026-10-13`), lengths are milliseconds, and ids are 64-bit integers.
Image fields hold absolute URLs, or `null`.

## Authentication

There are two kinds of credentials for this API, both sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

**Sessions** come from logging in (`POST /v1/auth/login` with `username`
and `password`) or registering (`POST /v1/auth/register`). The `token` in
the answer is the session; it lasts 30 days from login (`expires_at`),
however much it is used, and may do everything the account can.
`POST /v1/auth/logout` ends it, or with `?all=true` every session of the
account. Some servers accept logins and registrations only from their own
apps; elsewhere, ask the user for an API token.

**API tokens** are for scripts and apps that should do less than the
account can. The user creates one with a session (`POST /v1/auth/tokens`,
with a `name`, `scopes` and optionally `expires_days`); its value is shown
in that answer only. A token may do what its scopes allow, and none
implies another:

| scope | allows |
| --- | --- |
| `scrobble` | `POST /v1/scrobble` and `POST /v1/now-playing`: all a player needs. The default when no scopes are given. |
| `read` | the account's own data: `GET /v1/user/me`, its feed, community charts, recommendations, loved tracks, tags, imports, linked accounts and settings |
| `write` | changing the account and acting as it: the profile, follows, loves, tags, bios, comments, image votes and uploads, imports, catalog refreshes, recommendation skips, reports |

**Routes that take a session only**, never an API token, so that a leaked
token can't outlive its revocation or take the account over: creating and
revoking API tokens, logging out, scrobbler credentials and authorizations
(`/v1/scrobbler/*`), linking accounts (`GET /v1/connect/{provider}` and its
callback), blocks and removed followers, the similarity setting
(`PUT /v1/user/me/similarity`), the account export and deletion.

`GET /v1/auth/tokens` takes any credential; with an API token it lists only
that token, which is how an app checks the token it was given.

Routes that say more to a signed-in viewer (whether the viewer follows an
account, the viewer's own private profile, accounts blocking the viewer
left out) take a session only, since how other accounts stand to the
account is a session's to see; the track page (`GET /v1/track/{id}`) also
takes a token with `read`, for its `loved` flag. Any other credential
counts as signed out there.

Third-party scrobblers don't use any of these: they take **scrobbler
tokens**, which only scrobble, love and tag (the **Scrobblers** and
**Scrobbler protocols** sections).

A missing, invalid or expired credential is a `401`; one that doesn't
allow the route is a `403` saying what it lacks.

## Errors

Every error of the native API has the same body:

```json
{ "error": "this API token lacks the `write` scope" }
```

The message is for people and may change; branch on the status code.

| status | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | invalid input: a parameter out of range, a malformed cursor or tag, a body that doesn't parse |
| `401` | no credential, or an invalid or expired one; a wrong password at login |
| `403` | not allowed: someone else's private profile, a token without the scope, a route that takes a session, a wrong password where one is asked again, an account that can't edit yet |
| `404` | no such thing, or one the viewer may not know exists (below) |
| `409` | a conflict: a cap reached, a stale bio edit, a state that forbids it (following an account you block) |
| `413` | a body too large |
| `422` | a scrobble refused: too old, in the future, too short, a duplicate; or a JSON body missing a field |
| `429` | a rate limit (below) |
| `500` | something failed on the server; the body says nothing more |
| `503` | a feature this server isn't set up for (Spotify or Last.fm linking, browser approval) |

## Rate limits

Every request counts against a limit per client address, 60 a minute by
default (each server sets its own), an IPv6 client counting by its /64.
Some actions have limits of their own on top, per account and per
address, counted in fixed windows (the hour, the day) whether or not the
action succeeds:

| action | per account | per address |
| --- | --- | --- |
| scrobbles (every API together) | a daily allowance, 3,000 by default, until midnight UTC | |
| password logins (native and scrobbler APIs) | | 20 in 15 minutes, 10 of them for one username |
| image uploads | 20 an hour | 30 an hour |
| follows | 100 an hour; 3 new follows of the same account a day | 300 an hour |
| blocks, unblocks and removed followers | 200 an hour; 3 blocks of the same account a day | 600 an hour |
| loves and unloves (every API together) | 300 an hour | 1,000 an hour |
| bio edits and reverts | 30 an hour; 50 revisions, 3 of one bio, in 24 hours | 60 an hour |
| tag changes (every API together) | 120 an hour | 300 an hour |
| reports | 20 an hour | 60 an hour |
| account exports | 3 a day | 10 a day |
| account deletion attempts | 5 an hour | 10 an hour |
| live streams open at once | 20 per signed-in viewer | 50 |
| scrobbler API requests | 120 a minute | |

Past a limit the answer is `429` with the usual error body, without a
`Retry-After` header: wait for the window to end (the next minute, hour or
UTC day) rather than retrying at once. Conditional requests answered `304`
count too.

## Pagination

Lists come in pages, in one of two ways:

- **Cursors**, for lists that grow at the top (followers, blocks, loved
  tracks, the feed, a bio's history, your tags): pass `limit`, then the
  previous page's `next` as `before` for the page after it. `next` is
  `null` on the last page. A cursor is opaque; an invalid one is a `400`.
  Entries the viewer may not see are skipped, so a page can hold fewer
  than `limit` entries and still have a next one.
- **Offsets**, for ranked lists (charts, rankings, similar artists,
  recommendations, a tag's entities): pass `limit` and `offset`; the page
  says how many entries there are in all (`total`). A negative `offset` is
  a `400`; past the end, the page is empty.

`limit` is brought within each route's range (1 to its maximum) rather
than refused. Recent scrobbles page by time instead: `before` takes the
`played_at` of the last scrobble seen.

## Caching

Routes whose answers can be reused say so:

| route | `Cache-Control` | validator |
| --- | --- | --- |
| global rankings | `public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=300` | `ETag` |
| similar artists | `public, max-age=3600, stale-while-revalidate=3600` | `ETag` |
| an entity's tags, a tag's entities | `public, max-age=300` | `ETag` |
| a user's charts | `private, max-age=60`, `Vary: Authorization` | `ETag` |
| community charts | `private, max-age=60` | `ETag` |
| recommendations | `private, no-cache` | `ETag` |
| the feed, the account export | `no-store` | |
| uploaded images | `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` | |

Send an `ETag` back in `If-None-Match`; while nothing changed the answer
is `304 Not Modified` with no body. Tags are weak (`W/"…"`): compression
changes the bytes, not the content.

## Who sees what

A profile is either public or private, and the rules below hold on every
route, the scrobbler APIs included.

- **Private profiles** are their owner's alone. The profile and
  everything under it (recent scrobbles, top lists, charts, the heatmap,
  follow lists, loved tracks, tags, taste neighbours, the live stream)
  answer `403` to everyone else, followers included: following takes no
  approval.
- **Blocks.** An account that blocks the signed-in viewer doesn't exist
  for it: its profile and routes answer `404`, exactly as for a missing
  account, and it is left out of every list of people. Nobody is told who
  blocks them. The blocker still sees the blocked account's profile, with
  `blocking: true`.
- **Accounts waiting to be deleted** answer `404` and appear nowhere,
  until they are restored or erased.
- **Lists of people** (followers, following, listeners, search, comments,
  image candidates, taste neighbours) name public accounts only, but for
  the viewer's own entry, and leave out accounts blocking the viewer or
  blocked by it and accounts waiting to be deleted.
- **Authors.** Comments, uploaded images and bio revisions keep their
  author's name whatever the profile's privacy: they were published for
  everyone. A bio revision's `author` is `null` when its author is waiting
  to be deleted, blocks the viewer or is blocked by it.
- **Counts that add up everyone** include private accounts, unnamed:
  catalog play counts, follower counts, rankings, tag counts. Those that
  could stand for a handful of people are held back below a minimum of
  distinct accounts set by the server: a track's, artist's or album's
  `scrobble_count` is then `null`, and rankings, tag lists and community
  charts leave the entry out (community charts state the minimum as
  `min_listeners`).

At most 1000 entries; paged by `limit` (50 by default, 200 at most) and `offset`.

A ranking, once computed, is reused for 5 minutes by every request covering the same accounts and days, so pages of one chart agree and positions are that old at most; following or unfollowing, or an account turning private, makes another. Pages carry a weak `ETag` and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=60`: send the tag back in `If-None-Match` for a 304 while the ranking is the same.

tags.description:
Registering, logging in and out, and the account's API tokens (the
introduction's **Authentication** section explains sessions, tokens and
scopes).

- `POST /v1/auth/register` takes `username` (2 to 30 ASCII letters,
  digits and `_ - .`, starting and ending with a letter or digit), `email`,
  `password` (12 to 128 characters mixing at least three of lowercase,
  uppercase, digits and symbols, not containing the username or email)
  and an optional `display_name`; it answers `201` with a session, `409`
  when the username or email is taken.
- `POST /v1/auth/login` takes `username` and `password` and answers a
  session (`token`, `expires_at`); `account_restored` is `true` when the
  login cancelled the account's deletion. A wrong password or unknown user
  is a `401`.
- `POST /v1/auth/logout` ends the session (`?all=true`: every session of
  the account).
- `POST /v1/auth/tokens` (session) creates an API token: `name` (1 to 100
  characters), `scopes` (default `["scrobble"]`; an unknown scope or an
  empty list is a `400`) and `expires_days` (1 to 3,650; never expires
  when left out). The `token` is in this answer only.
  `GET /v1/auth/tokens` lists them without their values;
  `DELETE /v1/auth/tokens/{id}` (session) revokes one at once.

```json
{ "token": "3d0b1f7c-1c2e-4f61-9a43-5d6e2b8f9a10", "user_id": 812, "username": "alice",
  "expires_at": "2026-11-15T10:41:07Z", "account_restored": false }
```

A profile (`GET /v1/user/{username}`) is the account's public face: its
names, avatar, bio, scrobble count and follow counts. Usernames match
whatever their case. `GET /v1/user/me` is the signed-in account's own,
private or not.

```json
{
  "id": 70, "username": "ana", "display_name": "Ana", "bio": null,
  "image_url": "https://scrobblr.example/uploads/avatars/3f/3f2a….jpg",
  "website_url": null, "country": null, "scrobble_count": 4127,
  "is_private": false, "is_verified": false,
  "last_seen_at": "2026-10-13T10:41:07Z", "created_at": "2025-02-01T18:20:00Z",
  "is_following": true, "follows_you": false, "blocking": false,
  "followers_count": 12, "following_count": 35,
  "scrobble_breakdown": { "verified": 3990, "unverified": 137, "suspect": 2,
                          "no_data": 120, "pending": 15, "duplicates": 41 }
}
```

- `is_following`, `follows_you` and `blocking` describe the signed-in
  viewer's relation to the account, and are `null` signed out and on the
  viewer's own profile.
- `followers_count` and `following_count` count every follow, private
  accounts' included; the lists name only public ones.
- `scrobble_count` leaves out duplicates (one listen reported more than
  once); `scrobble_breakdown` splits it into `verified` and `unverified`
  plays (`suspect`, `no_data`, and `pending`, not checked yet).

**Settings** (`PATCH /v1/user/me`, `write`): `display_name` (40
characters at most), `bio` (1,000), `image_url` and `is_private`. Fields
left out stay as they are; an empty string clears one. `image_url` takes
an `https://` URL elsewhere; an uploaded avatar goes through
`POST /v1/user/me/avatar` (a multipart `image` field, re-encoded as a
JPEG of 512 pixels a side at most; the **Images** section has the limits),
and sending back the current avatar's URL leaves it as it is. Turning
private takes effect at once: others' live streams of the profile close.

**Listening** (the **Scrobbles** section): recent scrobbles, top artists
and tracks, the activity heatmap and a live stream of now playing, each as
visible as the profile.
tags.name: Users

tags.description:
A user can take their data with them and delete their account. Both
routes take a session, never an API token: a leaked token mustn't carry
the account away or delete it.

**Export** (`GET /v1/user/me/export`) streams a ZIP archive of everything
the server holds about the account, read as it is sent:

| file | |
| --- | --- |
| `README.txt` | what the files are |
| `account.json` | the profile and settings, follows, blocks made and followers removed, comments, uploads and likes, sessions, API tokens and scrobbler credentials (without their values), linked accounts (without their tokens), imports, now playing, the similarity setting, recommendations and taste neighbours as last computed, skipped recommendations, reports made, and `not_included`: what is left out, and why |
| `scrobbles.csv`, `scrobbles.json` | every scrobble, oldest first, with its source, client, import and `status` |
| `loved_tracks.csv`, `loved_tracks.json` | every loved track, with when and how it was loved |
| `tags.json` | every tag the user put on something |
| `bio_edits.json` | every bio revision the user wrote, with its text and status |
| `uploads/` | the avatar and artwork the user uploaded |

Nothing is stored on the server; a broken download is asked for again.
3 exports a day per account, 10 per address (`429`); while other exports
are running the answer can be `503`: try again in a few minutes. The
answer is `application/zip` with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

**Deletion** (`POST /v1/user/me/delete`) takes the account's `password`
and its username typed out as `confirm`:

```json
{ "password": "…", "confirm": "alice" }
```

It answers `202` with `delete_after`, when the account will be erased. A
wrong password is a `403`, a `confirm` that isn't the username a `400`; 5
attempts an hour per account, 10 per address.

- **At once**: every session, API token, scrobbler credential and linked
  account is revoked, imports stop, and the account disappears: its
  profile and routes answer `404`, and it leaves every list.
- **Until `delete_after`** (7 days by default): logging in with the
  password (`POST /v1/auth/login`) restores the account, history, follows
  and loves included, and says so (`account_restored: true`); credentials
  and linked accounts have to be made again. Scrobbler apps' logins never
  restore it. The username and email stay taken.
- **Then** the server erases everything about the account. Its plays
  leave catalog counts and rankings; published bio revisions stay without
  an author; artwork it uploaded that an artist or album shows stays as
  the catalog's. The username and email can be taken again.
tags.name: Account

tags.description:
A user links accounts elsewhere: **Spotify**, which the server then polls
for what the user played and scrobbles it, and **Last.fm**, which proves
the user owns the account whose history they import. Linking is a browser
flow started and finished by the same session (never an API token):

1. `GET /v1/connect/{provider}` (`spotify` or `lastfm`) answers an
   `authorize_url`; send the user's browser there.
2. The provider sends the browser back to the web app's
   `/connect/{provider}/callback` with a `state` and Spotify's `code` or
   Last.fm's `token` in the query.
3. The web app finishes with `POST /v1/connect/{provider}/callback`,
   `{ "state": "…", "code": "…" }` (or `"token"`), within 10 minutes and
   with the session of the user who started: a `state` belonging to
   another user, used or expired is a `400`; an account already linked to
   another Scrobblr user a `409`.

`GET /v1/connect` (`read`) lists the linked accounts, never their tokens;
`DELETE /v1/connect/{provider}` (`write`) unlinks one, and polling stops.
A server without a provider's keys answers `503`.
tags.name: Connected accounts

tags.description:
Users bring their Last.fm history over: loved tracks first, then every
scrobble. The server runs the import in the background.

1. **Link the Last.fm account** (**Connected accounts** section), which
   proves the user owns it.
2. **Start** with `POST /v1/import/lastfm` (`write`; a body
   `{ "full": true }` is optional): `202` with the import. `400` without a
   linked Last.fm account, `409` while another import runs, `429` within a
   day of the last one, `503` when the server has no Last.fm key.
3. **Follow** it with `GET /v1/imports/{id}` (or the 20 latest,
   `GET /v1/imports`; `read`) until `status` is `done`, `failed` or
   `cancelled`. `DELETE /v1/imports/{id}` (`write`) stops it after the page
   in flight; what was imported stays.

```json
{
  "id": 42, "provider": "lastfm", "external_user": "ana_fm", "verified": true,
  "status": "running", "error_code": null, "error_message": null,
  "window_from": null, "window_to": "2026-10-13T10:00:00Z",
  "total_expected": 31921, "fetched": 12000, "imported": 11890,
  "duplicates": 104, "skipped": 6, "oldest_played_at": "2024-02-11T21:04:00Z",
  "loved_total": 132, "loved_imported": 130, "loved_done": true, "loved_error": null,
  "retrying_at": null, "created_at": "2026-10-13T10:00:00Z",
  "started_at": "2026-10-13T10:00:05Z", "finished_at": null
}
```

- **Progress**: `fetched` against `total_expected` (known after the first
  page), `imported` new, `duplicates` already here (an earlier import, or
  the same listen scrobbled live), `skipped` invalid entries,
  `oldest_played_at` how far back it has reached. An import resumes after
  any interruption; `retrying_at` is set while it waits out a Last.fm
  error.
- **Again later**: a new import reads only what came after the last
  completed one (two weeks before its end, for late scrobbles); `full`
  reads everything. Neither creates duplicates.
- **Failures** (`error_code`): `user_not_found`, `history_hidden` (the
  Last.fm profile hides its listening and the account wasn't linked),
  `cap_reached` (the server's limit of imported scrobbles),
  `lastfm_unavailable` (Last.fm kept failing), `lastfm_error`.
- **Loved tracks** come first and add to the user's loves (up to 50,000);
  a love taken back here stays taken back on a later import, unless
  `full`. `loved_error` says why they stopped short, and the scrobbles go
  on.
- **Imported plays** show on the profile and in its charts like any other,
  and don't count in global rankings.
tags.name: Imports

tags.description:
A scrobble is one listen: what played and when it started. Players send
them with a session or a token with the `scrobble` scope, the only scope a
player needs.

```http
POST /v1/scrobble HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "track": "Teardrop",
  "artist": "Massive Attack",
  "album": "Mezzanine",
  "played_at": "2026-10-13T10:41:07Z",
  "duration_ms": 330000,
  "listened_ms": 165000,
  "source": "my-player"
}
```

The answer is `201` with the scrobble's `id` and `played_at`.

- **When to scrobble**: once the track has played for half its length or
  4 minutes, whichever comes first, and at least 30 seconds, as Last.fm
  clients do. A play reporting `listened_ms` under both 30 seconds and half
  of `duration_ms` is refused.
- **What to send**: `track` and `artist` (at most 300 characters each, as
  `album`), `played_at` when the track started, and whatever else is known:
  `duration_ms` (lengths outside 1 ms to 24 hours count as unknown),
  `listened_ms`, `featured_artists` (up to 16, in billing order; the main
  artist is `artist`), `source` (the player's name, cut to 100 characters)
  and `recording_mbid`, a MusicBrainz recording id the server checks
  against the title and artist before using it. Lengths and listened time
  help the server check plays.
- **Refused with `422`**: a play more than 30 days old (bring older
  history over with a Last.fm import), one more than 5 minutes in the
  future, an empty title or artist, a listen too short, and a duplicate:
  the same track within 30 seconds of a scrobble already stored, which
  is how retries and several players reporting one listen look.
  Duplicates are safe to send; a client should drop a play the server
  refused with any `4xx` but `429`.
- **The daily allowance**: each account records a number of scrobbles per
  UTC day (3,000 by default), counted across every API; past it, `429`
  until midnight UTC. Refused plays don't count.

**Now playing** (`POST /v1/now-playing`, `204`): the track starting now,
with the same fields but `played_at` and `listened_ms`. It shows on the
profile and its live stream until the track would end (5 minutes without
a length), or until the next update.

**Afterwards** every play is checked against the account's other plays.
Recent scrobbles carry the outcome as `status`: `counted`; `suspect`, more
listening than the time allows (several players at once, a script);
`no_data`, a track whose length nobody knows yet; `null`, not checked yet,
for a minute or so. Profiles count every play but the duplicates the check
finds; `scrobble_breakdown` on a profile says how many are verified.
tags.name: Scrobbling

tags.description:
What a settings page needs to manage third-party scrobblers (the
**Scrobbler protocols** section), all with a session, never an API token:

- `POST /v1/scrobbler/tokens` with a `name` creates a scrobbler token,
  shown once in the answer (`token`). `legacy_auth` is `false` when the
  server can't keep the MD5 that Audioscrobbler 1.2 players need: such a
  token works everywhere else.
- `GET /v1/scrobbler/credentials` lists the tokens and the Last.fm
  sessions apps obtained (name, kind, API key, dates), never their
  secrets; `DELETE /v1/scrobbler/credentials/{id}` revokes one, signing its
  app out at once.
- **Approving an app in the browser.** A Last.fm-style app sends the user
  to `/api/auth/`, which forwards to the web app's
  `/scrobbler/authorize` with the same query. With `?api_key=…&token=…`
  (desktop apps), the page shows `GET /v1/scrobbler/authorizations/{token}`
  (which API key asks, and whether the request is pending) and approves
  with `POST /v1/scrobbler/authorizations/{token}/approve`; the app's next
  `auth.getSession` gets its session key. With `?api_key=…&cb=…` (web
  apps), `POST /v1/scrobbler/authorizations` with `api_key` and
  `callback` approves at once and answers the `redirect_url` to send the
  browser to.
tags.name: Scrobblers

tags.description:
Scrobblr speaks the protocols existing scrobblers already know: the
Last.fm API (as Libre.fm and other GNU FM servers do), the older
Audioscrobbler 1.2 protocol, and ListenBrainz's. Most apps that let you
change the server need only the server URL and a token. These endpoints
live at the root of the API's address, and answer any web page (CORS).

## Setting up an app

**Make a scrobbler token**: in Scrobblr's settings, under Scrobblers,
create a token named after the app (`POST /v1/scrobbler/tokens`). It is
shown once. A scrobbler token scrobbles, loves and tags, and nothing else;
it never works on the native API, and revoking it signs the app out. Use
it wherever an app asks for a ListenBrainz token or an Audioscrobbler
password, and in Last.fm-style apps instead of your password: your
password then never leaves Scrobblr (some servers accept only tokens
there).

**Point the app at Scrobblr** (`https://scrobblr.example` stands for the
server's API address):

| app | choose | server URL | sign in with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Web Scrobbler | ListenBrainz, custom API URL | `https://scrobblr.example/1/submit-listens` | the token |
| Pano Scrobbler | GNU FM | `https://scrobblr.example/2.0/` | your username and the token |
| Pano Scrobbler | ListenBrainz, custom | `https://scrobblr.example/` | the token |
| mpris-scrobbler | `libre.fm` with `--url` | `https://scrobblr.example` | approve in the browser |
| Audioscrobbler 1.2 players (mpdscribe, Quod Libet's plugin, DeaDBeeF…) | custom submission URL | `https://scrobblr.example/` | your username and the token |
| other ListenBrainz clients | custom ListenBrainz server | `https://scrobblr.example/`, `…/1/` or `…/1/submit-listens`, whichever form the app asks for | the token |

Any other app with a setting for a Libre.fm or GNU FM server, a custom
Audioscrobbler 1.2 handshake URL or a custom ListenBrainz server should
work the same way. Apps that only talk to last.fm itself (Spotify's
Last.fm connection, streaming services' integrations, Web Scrobbler's
Last.fm and Libre.fm scrobblers) can't be pointed elsewhere: use
Scrobblr's own apps or its Spotify connection. Some Last.fm-style desktop
apps open a browser page to approve them; it is on the Scrobblr website:
sign in there and approve the app.

## What to expect

- Scrobbles go through the same checks as Scrobblr's own apps (the
  **Scrobbling** section). Sending a scrobble again (retries, an offline
  cache) records it once and counts as accepted.
- Only plays from the last 14 days are accepted, as on Last.fm; older ones
  are ignored. Bring older history over with the Last.fm import. A device
  clock up to 5 minutes fast is fine; more and its scrobbles are ignored.
- Limits: the account's daily allowance (3,000 by default), shared with
  every other API; 50 scrobbles per request (1,000 for a ListenBrainz
  import); 120 requests a minute per account; and the native limits on
  loves and tag changes.
- **Loves**: Last.fm apps love and unlove (`track.love`, `track.unlove`);
  a track the server hasn't seen is added to the catalog, as scrobbling it
  would. Audioscrobbler 1.2 players that rate a play as loved (`r=L`) love
  its track. ListenBrainz apps love through recording feedback (below).
  Loves show on your profile, as private as it is, and nowhere else.
- **Tags**: Last.fm apps add and remove your tags (`artist.addTags`,
  `.removeTag` and the same for albums and tracks) and read them back;
  tagging something the server has never seen is refused (error 6) rather
  than adding it to the catalog.
- **Web Scrobbler can't love tracks on Scrobblr.** Its Last.fm scrobbler
  talks only to last.fm, and its ListenBrainz scrobbler sends loves to
  listenbrainz.org itself, whatever server you set, with your Scrobblr
  token: listenbrainz.org refuses it, but the token has been sent there.
  If you scrobble from Web Scrobbler with a Scrobblr token, turn off
  "Love/unlove tracks through players" in its options (on by default) and
  don't press its love button; love from Scrobblr or another app instead.
- Pano Scrobbler shows track and artist info, bios and top tags from
  last.fm itself whatever server you set; Scrobblr's are on its own pages,
  and in `artist.getInfo` and the `getTopTags` methods for apps that ask
  the server.

## Last.fm API (`/2.0/`)

Requests as Last.fm's: a `method`, parameters in the query string or a
form body, answers in Last.fm's XML, or JSON with `format=json`, errors
with Last.fm's codes.

- **Signing in**: `auth.getMobileSession` (POST) with the username and a
  scrobbler token as the password (or the account password, where the
  server allows it) answers a session key; with a token, the session key
  is the token itself. The browser flow: `auth.getToken`, then send the
  user to `/api/auth/?api_key=…&token=…` (or `?api_key=…&cb=…` for the web
  flow) to approve, then `auth.getSession`. A session key (`sk`) is bound
  to the `api_key` it was issued to.
- **Signatures** (`api_sig`) are checked for API keys whose secret the
  server knows; others are accepted unless the server requires known keys.
  The credential is what authenticates, never the signature.
- **Methods**: `track.scrobble` (POST, up to 50 as `artist[i]`, `track[i]`,
  `timestamp[i]`…), `track.updateNowPlaying` (POST), `track.love`,
  `track.unlove` (POST), `track.getInfo` (by `artist` and `track` or
  `mbid`; `userloved` and `userplaycount` for a `username`, or the
  session's user, whose profile may be seen), `artist.getInfo` (the
  community bio, top tags, `userplaycount`), `artist.addTags`,
  `album.addTags`, `track.addTags` (POST, `tags` comma-separated, 10 at
  most), `.removeTag` (POST), `.getTags` (a user's tags on it), `.getTopTags`
  (the tags shown on it), `user.getInfo`, `user.getRecentTracks`
  (`extended=1` for the artist as an object and `loved`; 200 a page at
  most), `user.getLovedTracks` (1,000 a page at most), `user.getTopTags`.
  There are no `listeners` counts, and `playcount` is left out where the
  native API's count would be `null`.
- **Not served**: tag pages (`tag.*`), `album.getInfo`, charts, friends,
  library and similar-artist methods (error 3).
- **Visibility**: as on the native API. A private profile answers error
  17 but to its own session; an account blocking the session's account,
  waiting to be deleted or missing answers error 6.
- **Errors**: 6 invalid parameters (also a cap reached, an invalid tag, an
  unknown artist or track), 3 an unknown method, 4, 9, 10 and 13
  authentication (a suspended account's tagging too), 29 a rate limit, 16
  temporarily unavailable.

## Audioscrobbler 1.2

The handshake (`GET /?hs=true&p=1.2&u=USER&t=TIMESTAMP&a=AUTH`, also at
`/1.2/`) takes the username and `md5(md5(token) + timestamp)`, within 5
minutes of the server's clock: it needs a scrobbler token made while the
server could keep its MD5 (`legacy_auth` true when created). It answers a
session id and the now-playing (`/1.2/nowplaying`) and submission
(`/1.2/submissions`) URLs. Submissions take up to 50 plays (`a[i]`,
`t[i]`, `i[i]`, `o[i]`, `r[i]`, `l[i]`, `b[i]`, `n[i]`, `m[i]`); `r[i]=S`
or `B` drops a play, `L` loves its track. Sessions last a day after their
last use and end when the token is revoked.

## ListenBrainz (`/1/`)

Authenticated with the scrobbler token as `Authorization: Token <token>`.

- `POST /1/submit-listens`: `listen_type` `single`, `playing_now` or
  `import` (1,000 listens at most), `track_metadata` with `artist_name`,
  `track_name`, `release_name` and `additional_info` (`duration_ms`,
  `recording_mbid`, `submission_client`…). With `return_msid`, a
  `playing_now` answers the track's `recording_msid`.
- `GET /1/validate-token`: whether the token is valid, and its user.
- `POST /1/feedback/recording-feedback`: `recording_mbid` or
  `recording_msid`, and `score` 1 (love), 0 or -1 (take a love back; hates
  aren't kept). A love of a recording the catalog doesn't have is a `404`
  (scrobble it first).
- `GET /1/feedback/user/{user_name}/get-feedback` (`count` 25 by default,
  1,000 at most, `offset`, `score`, `metadata=true`): the user's loves,
  newest first. `get-feedback-for-recordings` (GET or POST,
  `recording_msids`, `recording_mbids`, 1,000 at most): 1 or 0 for each.
  Both are as visible as the profile and take no token.
- A recording MBID names the track MusicBrainz matched to it, or one a
  client named it for. An MSID is one this server handed out
  (`recording_msid`), never listenbrainz.org's.
- Not served: who loved a recording, and how many (loves have no public
  count), and the rest of ListenBrainz's API.
tags.name: Scrobbler protocols

tags.description:
A user's listening, as visible as the profile: public, or the owner's
alone when private.

- **Recent scrobbles** (`GET /v1/user/{username}/recent`): newest first,
  `limit` 50 by default and 200 at most; for older ones pass the last
  `played_at` seen as `before`. Each carries `status` (as in the
  **Scrobbling** section) and `loved`, whether the user loves the track
  now. Duplicates are left out.
- **Top artists and tracks** (`/top-artists`, `/top-tracks`): the most
  played over a `period` (`limit` 10 by default, 50 at most); the
  **Charts** section has the paged, ranged version of the same lists.
- **Heatmap** (`/heatmap`): plays per UTC day over the last 365 days,
  oldest first, days without plays left out.
- **Live** (`/live`): a Server-Sent Events stream of what the user plays.
  The first event is the current state (`null` when nothing plays), then
  one per update, each a `NowPlayingRich`. An entry that ends sends no
  event: compare its `expires_at` with the clock. An idle stream sends a
  comment every 15 seconds. A block closes the blocked account's streams
  of the blocker, and a profile turning private closes everyone's but its
  owner's.

```text
GET /v1/user/ana/live
Accept: text/event-stream

data: null

data: {"track_id":1841,"track_title":"Teardrop","artist_name":"Massive Attack","album_title":"Mezzanine","album_image":null,"artist_image":null,"started_at":"2026-10-13T10:41:07Z","expires_at":"2026-10-13T10:46:37Z","source":"my-player"}
```
tags.name: Scrobbles

tags.description:
**A user's charts** (`GET /v1/user/{username}/charts/{artists,tracks,albums}`,
public, as visible as the profile): the account's most played artists,
tracks or albums over a period.

| parameter | | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `period` | `7d` (default), `30d`, `90d`, `12m` (365 days), `all` | UTC days ending today, today included |
| `from`, `to` | `YYYY-MM-DD`, both included | instead of `period`: both or neither, `to` not after today, 366 days at most |
| `limit`, `offset` | 50 by default, 200 at most | |

```json
{
  "period": "30d", "from": "2026-09-14", "to": "2026-10-13",
  "total": 212, "offset": 0, "limit": 2,
  "entries": [
    { "album_id": 31, "album_title": "Mezzanine", "artist_id": 97,
      "artist_name": "Massive Attack", "image_url": null,
      "play_count": 41, "unverified_count": 3 },
    { "album_id": 8, "album_title": "Dummy", "artist_id": 12,
      "artist_name": "Portishead", "image_url": null,
      "play_count": 30, "unverified_count": 0 }
  ]
}
```

`period` is `null` for a custom range, `from` is `null` for `all`. Plays
are the profile's: duplicates left out, plays the server couldn't verify
in, counted again in `unverified_count`. A track counts for the one album
the catalog files it under, whichever release it was played from. A page
can lag the newest plays by up to an hour; send its `ETag` back to get a
`304` while it hasn't changed.

The older `GET /v1/user/{username}/top-artists` and `/top-tracks` take
`period` as `7days`, `1month`, `3months`, `6months`, `1year` or `overall`
and a `limit`.

**Community charts** (`GET /v1/user/me/community/{artists,tracks,albums}`,
`read`): what the accounts you follow play, ranked as the global rankings
are (**Rankings** section): by listeners, then plays, both whole numbers
and weighted towards real listening. The same parameters, but no `all`:
a range starts within the last year.

```json
{
  "period": "7d", "from": "2026-10-07", "to": "2026-10-13",
  "following": 64, "accounts": 64, "min_listeners": 5,
  "total": 18, "offset": 0, "limit": 50,
  "entries": [
    { "position": 1, "track_id": 1841, "track_title": "Teardrop", "artist_id": 97,
      "artist_name": "Massive Attack", "album_image": null, "listeners": 9, "plays": 14 }
  ]
}
```

- `following` is how many of the accounts you follow the chart may cover
  (public, not waiting to be deleted); `accounts` how many it covers: the
  most recently active, every one over a week, fewer over longer ranges
  (40 over a year).
- An entry needs `min_listeners` of those accounts: following fewer
  accounts than that gives an empty chart. Nothing names an account.
- A chart is kept for 5 minutes, and pages and repeat views read it;
  following or unfollowing someone makes a new one.
tags.name: Charts

tags.description:
A user can love a track, as on Last.fm: a list on the profile and a heart
on the track's page, in recent scrobbles and in the feed. Loves are what a
user says, not listening: they show on the profile and count nowhere else
(no rankings, recommendations or "loved by" numbers).

| route | access | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/track/{id}/love` | `write` | `204`, also when loved already (the first `loved_at` stands); `404` not in the catalog; `409` at 50,000 loved tracks |
| `DELETE /v1/track/{id}/love` | `write` | `204`, also when not loved; `404` not in the catalog |
| `GET /v1/user/{username}/loved` | public, as visible as the profile | a page, newest love first |
| `GET /v1/user/me/loved` | `read` | the same, whatever the profile's privacy |

```json
{
  "entries": [
    { "track_id": 1841, "track_title": "Teardrop", "artist_id": 97,
      "artist_name": "Massive Attack", "album_id": 31, "album_title": "Mezzanine",
      "album_image": null, "artist_image": null,
      "loved_at": "2026-10-13T10:41:07.123456Z" }
  ],
  "total": 132,
  "next": "1760352067123456.1841"
}
```

Pages go by cursor (`limit` 50, at most 200; `before`); `total` counts
every loved track. `GET /v1/track/{id}` says whether the viewer loves it
(`loved`, `null` signed out); recent scrobbles and feed entries say
whether the account that played the track loves it now. Now playing
carries `track_id`, so an app can love what is playing.

The native routes love by track id and create nothing. Scrobbler apps
love by artist and title through the Last.fm and ListenBrainz protocols,
and a Last.fm import brings the account's loved tracks over (the
**Scrobbler protocols** and **Imports** sections).
tags.name: Loved tracks

tags.description:
**Follows** take no approval and open nothing: a private profile stays
its owner's alone, followers included.

| route | access | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/user/{username}/follow` | `write` | `204`, also when already following; `400` yourself; `404` no such account; `409` at the cap, an account you block, or one that removed you from its followers in the last 30 days |
| `DELETE /v1/user/{username}/follow` | `write` | `204` |
| `GET /v1/user/{username}/followers`, `/following` | public | a page, newest follow first (`FollowPage`) |
| `GET /v1/user/{username}/friends` | public | the 100 most recent of each list |

An account may follow 2,000 others. Follow lists page by cursor (`limit`
50, at most 200; `before`); each entry is a profile with `followed_at`,
and for a signed-in viewer `is_following` (the viewer follows it) and
`follows_you` (it follows the viewer).

**Blocks** (session only, never an API token):

| route | |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/user/{username}/block` | `204`, also when already blocking; `400` yourself; `404` no such account; `409` at the cap (10,000) |
| `DELETE /v1/user/{username}/block` | `204`, also when not blocking |
| `GET /v1/user/me/blocks` | the accounts you block, newest first (`BlockPage`); a private one shows its username only |
| `DELETE /v1/user/me/followers/{username}` | remove a follower without blocking it: `204` |

A block ends the follows between the two accounts both ways, and neither
can follow the other while it stands. The blocked account, signed in,
finds no such account: every route of the blocker answers `404` as for a
missing account, and the blocker is left out of every list it reads. It
is never told, but a public profile is anyone's to see signed out: a
block hides an account from an account, not from a person. A removed
follower keeps seeing your profile but can't follow you again for 30
days.

**The feed** (`GET /v1/user/me/feed`, `read`): the last 14 days of what
the accounts you follow played, newest first, from the public ones you
may see. Plays found suspect and duplicates are left out; plays not
checked yet are in with `status: null`.

```json
{
  "entries": [
    { "id": 912873, "played_at": "2026-10-13T10:41:07Z",
      "user": { "id": 70, "username": "ana", "display_name": "Ana", "image_url": null },
      "track_id": 1841, "track_title": "Teardrop", "artist_id": 97,
      "artist_name": "Massive Attack", "album_id": 31, "album_title": "Mezzanine",
      "album_image": null, "artist_image": null, "status": "counted", "loved": false }
  ],
  "next": "1760352067000000.912873"
}
```

Pages go by cursor (`limit` 50, at most 100; `before`) and stay where
they are however many plays arrive: poll the first page, and stop paging
back at an entry you already have (`id` is the scrobble's). `next` is
`null` once a page reaches the 14th day. There is no stream.

Community charts, of the accounts you follow, are in the **Charts**
section.
tags.name: Social

tags.description:
What listening says about artists and people: an artist's similar
artists, a user's taste neighbours (accounts that chose to be shown whose
listening is closest), and artists recommended to the signed-in user. The
server computes all three once a day and serves what it stored, minus what
changed since (plays, skips, blocks, privacy).

| route | access | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/artist/{id}/similar` | public | a page; `404` no such artist |
| `GET /v1/user/{username}/similar` | public, as visible as the profile | the taste neighbours; `404` unless the user shows them |
| `GET /v1/user/me/recommendations/artists` | `read` | a page |
| `POST /v1/user/me/recommendations/artists/{id}/skip` | `write` | hide an artist for 90 days: `204`; `404` no such artist |
| `DELETE /v1/user/me/recommendations/artists/{id}/skip` | `write` | show it again: `204` |
| `GET /v1/user/me/similarity` | `read` | the setting |
| `PUT /v1/user/me/similarity` | session | `{ "mode": "listed" }`; `400` an unknown mode |

**Similar artists** (`limit` 20, at most 50; `offset`): whose listeners
also play the artist, `score` from 0 to 1. `common_listeners` is a lower
bound (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, …), never an exact count. An artist with
too few listeners has none (`total: 0`); before the first daily run
`computed_at` is `null`. `stale` is `true` when the daily run is late (the
last results are still served). Cacheable for an hour, with an `ETag`.

```json
{
  "artist_id": 97, "computed_at": "2026-10-14T03:12:40Z", "stale": false,
  "total": 50, "offset": 0, "limit": 1,
  "entries": [
    { "position": 1, "artist_id": 12, "artist_name": "Portishead",
      "image_url": null, "score": 0.412, "common_listeners": 200 }
  ]
}
```

**Recommendations** (`limit` 20, at most 100; `offset`): artists the user
never played, ranked by how much the listeners of the user's artists play
them; `score` is relative to the first (1.0). `because` is the user's own
artist that counted most, `because_count` how many of the user's artists
led there. Artists played since the daily run, or skipped, are left out
at once. Imported history counts here, for the user's own results. Send
the `ETag` back to get a `304` while nothing changed.

```json
{
  "status": "ready", "computed_at": "2026-10-14T03:12:40Z", "stale": false,
  "total": 87, "offset": 0, "limit": 20,
  "entries": [
    { "position": 1, "artist_id": 31, "artist_name": "Tricky", "image_url": null,
      "score": 1.0, "because": { "artist_id": 97, "artist_name": "Massive Attack" },
      "because_count": 3 }
  ]
}
```

**Taste neighbours** (`limit` 10, at most 30): accounts that chose
`listed`, public, not blocking or blocked by the list's owner or the
viewer, with a `score`, how many artists they share and the three
counting most (`top_shared`). A user's own list is theirs whatever the
setting; someone else's is shown only when that user is `listed` (a `404`
otherwise, as for a missing user).

`status` (recommendations and neighbours): `ready`; `none`, too little
listening yet, or nobody close enough; `off`, the user turned similarity
off; `pending`, nothing computed yet.

**The setting** (`mode`):

| mode | the account's listening | shown as a taste neighbour | its own results |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listed` | counts, anonymously, in similar artists and others' recommendations | yes, while the profile is public | yes, and anyone may see its neighbours |
| `anonymous` (default) | counts, anonymously | never | yes, its own to see |
| `off` | not used | never | none |

`GET` answers `{ "mode": "anonymous", "shown": false, "changed_at": null }`
(`shown`: others see the account as a neighbour now). Leaving `listed`
removes the account from others' lists at once; `off` also deletes its own
results, and its anonymous part leaves similar artists at the next daily
run.
tags.name: Recommendations

tags.description:
Artists, albums and tracks, shared by everyone: created by whoever
scrobbles them first, then filled in by the server from MusicBrainz, Cover
Art Archive, Deezer and Last.fm (ids, lengths, release dates, images,
bios). Names and titles are kept as first scrobbled.

- `GET /v1/artist/{id}`, `/v1/album/{id}`, `/v1/track/{id}`: one entity by
  its id. A track lists its artist credits (`artists`: the main artist,
  then featured ones in billing order) and, for a signed-in viewer,
  whether it loves the track.
- `GET /v1/search?q=…`: artists, tracks and people at once; `type`
  `artist`, `track`, `user` or `all` (default), `limit` 10 by default and
  30 at most per kind; `q` is 1 to 200 characters. People are public
  profiles only, without accounts blocking the viewer or blocked by it.
- `GET /v1/artist/{id}/top-tracks`: its most played tracks across
  everyone (`limit` 10, at most 50).
- `GET /v1/artist/{id}/listeners`, `/v1/track/{id}/listeners`: the public
  profiles that play it most, with their play counts, as their profiles
  already show (`limit` 10, at most 50).
- **Counts**: `scrobble_count` adds up everyone's plays, private profiles'
  included, and is `null` for an entity fewer than a minimum of distinct
  accounts played (a new listener counts within the hour, today's plays
  from tomorrow). An album's count is its tracks'. `listener_count` is
  always `null`.
- **Albums**: each track counts for one album, the one the accounts
  playing it name most, whichever release a play came from; a track filed
  under no album is in no album chart.
- **Refreshing** (`POST /v1/{artist,album,track}/{id}/refresh`, `write`,
  `202`): asks the server to look the entity up again at the providers, in
  the background. An image chosen by the community is never replaced.

**Comments** on artists and tracks: `GET /v1/{artist,track}/{id}/comments`
(public, newest first, without accounts blocking the signed-in viewer or
blocked by it), `POST` with `{ "body": "…" }` (`write`, 1 to 2,000
characters, `201`), and `DELETE /v1/comments/{id}` for your own (`204`;
`404` for anyone else's). A comment shows its author's name whatever the
profile's privacy.
tags.name: Catalog

tags.description:
Users upload their avatar and propose artwork for artists and albums.
Every upload is a multipart body with one `image` file field:

```http
POST /v1/artist/97/image HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=x

--x
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="image"; filename="cover.png"
Content-Type: image/png

<bytes>
--x--
```

- **Formats**: JPEG, PNG or WebP, recognised from the file's contents, at
  most 8 MiB, 12,000 pixels a side and 40 megapixels. Anything else is a
  `400`, a larger body a `413`.
- **What is stored**: the server re-encodes every image as a JPEG, at
  most 512 pixels a side for avatars and 1,024 for artwork, transparency
  on white; nothing of the original file survives (EXIF and location data
  included). Image fields hold its URL, which never changes; a new image
  gets a new URL.
- **Limits**: 20 uploads an hour per account, 30 per address, refused
  ones included (`429`).

**Avatars** (`POST /v1/user/me/avatar`, `write`) replace the account's
avatar at once and answer with the updated profile; the previous uploaded
avatar is deleted.

**Artwork** works as on Last.fm: an upload
(`POST /v1/{artist,album}/{id}/image`, `write`) adds a candidate, which
its uploader likes. `GET /v1/{artist,album}/{id}/images` lists the
candidates, most liked first, with `has_voted` for the signed-in viewer and
`is_default` for the one shown; `POST` and `DELETE /v1/image/{id}/vote`
(`write`) like a candidate or take the like back, answering with the
refreshed list. The most liked candidate becomes the entity's image once
enough people like it, and then stays: a like taken back never takes an
image down, and the server's own lookups never replace it. A candidate
shows its uploader's username whatever the profile's privacy.
tags.name: Images

tags.description:
Artists and albums have a bio written by the community, as a wiki is:
every edit is a revision, kept for good with its author, time and summary,
and an earlier one can be restored.

| route | access | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/{artist,album}/{id}/bio` | public | the current text (`Bio`) |
| `GET /v1/{artist,album}/{id}/bio/history` | public | published revisions, newest first (`BioHistoryPage`) |
| `GET /v1/bio/revisions/{id}` | public | one revision with its text |
| `PUT /v1/{artist,album}/{id}/bio` | `write` | an edit: `200` published, `202` held for review |
| `POST /v1/{artist,album}/{id}/bio/revert` | `write` | restore an earlier revision: `200` |
| `POST /v1/reports` | `write` | report a revision or a tag: `204` |

```json
{
  "entity_type": "artist", "entity_id": 97, "revision_id": 5012,
  "body": "Massive Attack are a trip hop group from Bristol.\n\nFormed in 1988 …",
  "kind": "edit",
  "author": { "id": 812, "username": "alice", "display_name": "Alice", "image_url": null },
  "updated_at": "2026-10-15T14:02:11.408211Z", "locked": false, "revisions": 7
}
```

A revision (`BioRevision`) has its `id`, `parent_id` (the revision
current when it was written), `kind` (`edit`, `revert`, `import` from
Last.fm, `moderation`), `author`, `summary`, `body` (`null` in history
pages: fetch the revision), `length`, `reverted_to`, `status`
(`published`, `held`, `rejected`), `held_reason`, `hidden`, `current` and
`created_at`. History pages go by cursor (`limit` 50, at most 200;
`before`). Hidden revisions keep their place with `summary` and `body`
`null`.

**Editing.** `PUT` takes `body`, an optional `summary` (one line, 200
characters) and `base_revision_id`: the `revision_id` of the bio the text
was written over, `null` when it had none. If another revision came in
between, nothing is written: `409`, saying which revision is current, and
the client reads the bio again and merges. Sending the current text again
is a `400`. A revert takes `revision_id` (an earlier published revision of
the same bio), `base_revision_id` and `summary`. Both answer with the new
revision.

**The text** is plain: no HTML or Markdown. Show it as text, a paragraph
at each blank line, with `http://` and `https://` URLs as links marked
`rel="nofollow ugc noopener"`, never embedded or previewed. The server
normalizes line breaks and spacing and refuses (`400`) an empty text, more
than 10,000 characters, more than 5 links, and control, invisible or
bidirectional formatting characters.

**Who may edit:** an account some days after registering (a `403` says
from when), unless it can't edit for now (a `403` saying so) or the bio is
locked (`403`, the bio says `locked: true`). An edit that looks like spam
is held (`202`, with `held_reason`) until a moderator approves it: the bio
doesn't change, the edit isn't in the history, and only its author can
read it (`GET /v1/bio/revisions/{id}`). Reverts are never held. Limits are
in the introduction's rate limits.

**Authors** are named whatever their profile's privacy; `author` is `null`
for imported text and a moderator's revisions, and for an author waiting
to be deleted, blocking the viewer or blocked by it. After an account is
erased its published revisions stay, without an author.

**Reports** (`POST /v1/reports`) take a `revision_id`, or a `tag` (on the
entity `artist_id`, `album_id` or `track_id` names, or anywhere), a
`reason` (`spam`, `vandalism`, `offensive`, `personal_data`, `copyright`,
`other`) and an optional `note` (one line, 500 characters). Only what can
be seen can be reported (a `404` otherwise); reporting the same thing
again while the first report is open changes nothing. Nobody is told who
reported, and the reporter isn't told the outcome.

`GET /v1/artist/{id}` carries the current text as `bio`; an album has no
`bio` field: read its bio route.
tags.name: Bios

tags.description:
Users tag artists, albums and tracks, as on Last.fm. What a user tagged is
theirs and shows with their profile; what everyone sees on an entity is
the tags enough established accounts put there.

| route | access | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/{artist,album,track}/{id}/tags` | public | the tags shown on it (`TopTags`), most taggers first |
| `GET /v1/tag/{tag}/{artists,albums,tracks}` | public | the entities a tag is shown on (`TaggedEntityPage`) |
| `POST /v1/{artist,album,track}/{id}/tags` | `write` | `{ "tags": ["trip-hop"] }`: add up to 10 of yours; answers with your tags on it (`EntityTags`) |
| `DELETE /v1/{artist,album,track}/{id}/tags/{tag}` | `write` | remove one of yours: `204`, also when it wasn't there |
| `GET /v1/user/me/tags` | `read` | your tags, newest first (`UserTagPage`); `?artist=`, `album=` or `track=` for one entity |
| `GET /v1/user/{username}/tags` | public, as visible as the profile | the tags a user uses, and on how many entities (`UserTags`) |

```json
{ "entity_type": "artist", "entity_id": 97,
  "tags": [ { "name": "trip-hop", "taggers": 41 }, { "name": "electronic", "taggers": 12 } ] }
```

- **Names** are stored in one form: Unicode compatibility forms folded
  (full-width letters, ligatures), lowercase, single spaces, trimmed; 1 to
  40 characters of letters, digits, spaces and `- & ' . + ! _`, with at
  least one letter or digit. Anything else is a `400`, and so is a tag the
  server refuses. Paths take any spelling: `/v1/tag/Trip%20%20Hop/artists`
  is `trip hop`.
- **Caps**: 10 of your tags on one entity, 500 different tags on one
  entity, 50,000 taggings per account (`409`). An account that can't tag
  for now gets a `403`.
- **What everyone sees**: a tag shows on an entity once enough
  established accounts use it there; `taggers` is about how many, private
  accounts counted unnamed. New tags show within a minute or so; a tag
  below the minimum doesn't show at all, so your own tags on an entity
  (`GET /v1/user/me/tags?artist=…`) can be more than everyone sees.
- **Pages**: a tag's entities page by `limit` (50, at most 200) and
  `offset`, with `total`; your tags by cursor (`before`).
- **Caching**: both public reads send `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`
  and an `ETag`.

Tags aren't imported from Last.fm. Scrobbler apps tag through the Last.fm
protocol (**Scrobbler protocols** section), within the same caps and
limits.
tags.name: Tags

tags.description:
The server's global charts of artists and tracks (`GET /v1/rankings/artists`,
`GET /v1/rankings/tracks`), public, the same for everyone.

| parameter | | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `period` | `week` (default), `month`, `year` | the last 7, 30 or 365 UTC days, today included; anything else is a `400` |
| `limit`, `offset` | 50 by default, 200 at most | positions to skip; past the end, an empty page |

```json
{
  "period": "week", "from": "2026-10-04", "to": "2026-10-10",
  "computed_at": "2026-10-10T22:01:07.512Z", "stale": false,
  "total": 812, "offset": 0, "limit": 2,
  "entries": [
    { "position": 1, "track_id": 1841, "track_title": "Teardrop", "artist_id": 97,
      "artist_name": "Massive Attack", "album_image": null,
      "listeners": 412, "plays": 1290 },
    { "position": 2, "track_id": 77, "track_title": "Windowlicker", "artist_id": 12,
      "artist_name": "Aphex Twin", "album_image": null, "listeners": 398, "plays": 1517 }
  ]
}
```

- **Order**: by `listeners`, then `plays`, both whole numbers. They count
  real listening: plays that don't look like a person listening count
  less or not at all, and imported history doesn't count. They are not a
  sum of profiles' play counts, and no raw counts are served.
- **Who is in it**: every account, private ones included, never named.
  An artist or track with too few listeners is left out, so no position
  stands for one or two people.
- **Freshness**: rankings are computed in the background, the week's and
  month's every hour, the year's every day, and when the UTC day changes.
  `computed_at` says when, `from` and `to` which days. A refresh running
  late is served anyway with `stale: true`; before the first one, the
  answer is `404`. A page reads one stored ranking, so pages fetched across
  a refresh can repeat or skip a position (`computed_at` changes).
- **Caching**: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300,
  stale-while-revalidate=300` and an `ETag`; `If-None-Match` gets a `304`.

Artists' entries carry `artist_id`, `artist_name` and `image_url`; tracks'
the track, its artist, and the album cover as `album_image`.
tags.name: Rankings
